text:
Marathon Petroleum rose modestly today as oil prices stabilized after a volatile week. U.S. crude had plummeted nearly 8% last week on hopes of U.S.-Iran diplomatic talks, but those negotiations appear stalled—Trump rejected Iran's ceasefire proposal, and geopolitical tensions remain high. With U.S. oil at $96.41 and refineries operating at 94% capacity, the stock recovered a fraction of its recent losses, though it remains down sharply from $424 two weeks ago.

The broader backdrop remains uncertain for refiners. The sharp drop from mid-September reflects investor anxiety about oil supply: tensions with Iran could disrupt global crude flows, but they also keep prices elevated and volatile, making refining margins hard to predict. At current oil prices and high refinery utilization, the company isn't obviously cheaper or more profitable than it looked a month ago.
